# What this file demonstrates

This single file is a full showcase of the extension options and common book content.

For real book projects, keep book structure in `_quarto.yml` and split content into multiple files.

## Recommended _quarto.yml for a real book

```yaml
project:
  type: book

book:
  title: "My Book"
  author: "Your Name"
  chapters:
    - index.qmd
    - part: "Part I"
      chapters:
        - chapters/intro.qmd
        - chapters/methods.qmd
    - part: "Part II"
      chapters:
        - chapters/results.qmd
        - chapters/discussion.qmd
  appendices:
    - appendices/appendixA.qmd

format:
  bookly-typst:
    lang: en
    toc: true
    lof: true
    lot: true
    theme: modern
    tufte: false
```

## Code blocks

```python
from math import sqrt

values = [1, 4, 9]
roots = [sqrt(v) for v in values]
print(roots)
```

## Footnotes and links

Bookly works with standard markdown features like footnotes.[^example-footnote]

More info: [Quarto Typst docs](https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/typst.html)

[^example-footnote]: Footnotes are handled natively by Quarto + Typst.

## Appendix-style heading example

In a real book project, appendices should live in `appendices/*.qmd` and be declared under `book.appendices` in `_quarto.yml`.
